sources.title: Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, second edition
sources.locator: Full 683-page second-edition book PDF retrieved; the relevant sections were inspected in full. Chapter 3 §§3.1–3.2, printed pp. 33–40 / PDF pp. 51–58: Wolfe and strong Wolfe conditions, Lemma 3.1, Theorem 3.2 and its proof. Chapter 3 §3.5, printed pp. 56–61 / PDF pp. 74–79: bracketing/zoom line search. Chapter 5 §5.2, printed pp. 121–130 / PDF pp. 139–148: nonlinear CG and its Wolfe/Zoutendijk use. Chapter 7 §7.1, printed pp. 165–170 / PDF pp. 183–188: inexact Newton forcing residual, local rates, Newton–CG and negative-curvature safeguards.

contents.name: §3.1 Wolfe and strong Wolfe inequalities; Lemma 3.1 existence proof and strict accepted interval
contents.reason: The local definition records the exact sufficient-decrease and curvature inequalities, the strong-curvature variant, and the stipulated parameter range.

contents.name: §3.1 Lemma 3.1: a bounded-below descent ray has an interval of Wolfe and strong Wolfe steps
contents.reason: The local proof gives the ray domain, first-crossing argument, mean-value step, strict inequalities, and open accepted interval explicitly.

contents.name: §3.2 Theorem 3.2: complete Zoutendijk summability derivation and uniform-angle consequence
contents.reason: The local proof states the segment-wide gradient Lipschitz condition, derives the step lower bound, uses Armijo decrease, and telescopes against the lower bound.

contents.name: §3.2 equations (3.16)–(3.18): a uniform nonorthogonality condition implies gradient-norm convergence
contents.reason: The local corollary proves the summable nonnegative-sequence argument without adding a minimizer or iterate-convergence claim.

contents.name: §3.5 Wolfe line-search bracketing/zoom algorithm and reversed endpoint order
contents.reason: The authored procedure spells out deterministic expansion, bisection, domain and evaluation-budget statuses, and accepts only verified strong Wolfe steps.

contents.name: §3.3 Theorem 3.6: eventual unit Wolfe steps require convergence to a positive-definite critical point
contents.reason: This source result is retained as a boundary: the local root recurrence does not use it to assert automatic entry into the globalized full-step branch under invertibility alone.

contents.name: §5.2 nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrences and Theorem 5.7 use the Wolfe/Zoutendijk bound under method-specific hypotheses
contents.reason: The nonlinear conjugate-gradient algorithm and its direction-specific convergence argument are owned atomically by OPT14; this batch supplies only the general Wolfe/Zoutendijk premise and asserts no conjugate-gradient claim.

contents.name: §7.1 inexact Newton residual (7.2)–(7.3), Theorems 7.1–7.2, and Newton–CG Algorithm 7.1
contents.reason: The local algorithm makes the declared solver, shifted residual recomputation, descent safeguard, finite budgets, and failure returns explicit; no source termination guarantee is imported.

contents.name: §7.1 local forcing-sequence rates and the source's informal recurrence discussion
contents.reason: The local theorem supplies a complete invariant-tube proof for general root maps and states the exact unshifted full-step scope rather than borrowing the book's informal derivation.

contents.name: Finite capped adaptation of §3.5 bracketing/zoom: local checked-return and E+Z consequence
contents.reason: The established source-method context is already represented by the local algorithm. This added intermediate result proves consequences of its explicit local budgets and checks; no identical theorem in the reference, new external reading or new fetch is claimed.

contents.name: Finite capped adaptation of §7.1 Newton–CG: local termination, feasibility and separate count consequences
contents.reason: The established source-method context is already represented by the local algorithm. This added intermediate result proves consequences of its explicit local budgets and checks; no identical theorem in the reference, new external reading or new fetch is claimed.

sources.title: Ron S. Dembo, Stanley C. Eisenstat, and Trond Steihaug, Inexact Newton Methods, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 19 (1982), 400–408
sources.locator: Complete 10-page PDF of the 1982 paper fetched and inspected. The relative residual definition is on printed p. 401 / PDF pp. 2–3; Theorem 2.3 and its proof on pp. 402–403 / PDF pp. 3–4; Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.5 on pp. 404–407 / PDF pp. 5–8; the forcing-sequence counterexample is on p. 408 / PDF pp. 8–9.

contents.name: §1 equation (1.3): inexact Newton equation and relative linear-system residual
contents.reason: The unshifted branch uses this exact residual convention; shifted systems are separately checked against their own shifted operator.

contents.name: §2 Theorem 2.3 and proof: uniform forcing below one yields local linear convergence
contents.reason: The local remainder argument makes the norm, inverse bound, constants, and invariant neighborhood explicit instead of relying on the source proof alone.

contents.name: §3 Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.5: residual conditions for superlinear and higher-order convergence
contents.reason: The local proof derives linear, superlinear, and quadratic rates from its recurrence and preserves the required residual scaling.

contents.name: Appendix counterexample: a rapidly decreasing forcing sequence alone does not force the same higher order for the iterates
contents.reason: The theorem distinguishes eta tending to zero for superlinear convergence from eta=O(||F(x)||) for quadratic convergence, so it does not infer quadratic order from a fast eta sequence alone.
